source_refs.title: Update your iPhone or iPad - Apple Support
source_refs.section: Update your iPhone or iPad wirelessly
source_refs.applicability: iPhone; wireless update through Settings; power and Wi-Fi as stated on the page
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Keeping your software up to date is one of the most important things you can do to maintain your Apple product's security.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On iPhone: Back up your device to iCloud or a computer. Plug the device into a power source and connect to Wi-Fi. Open 'Settings.' Tap 'General.' Tap 'Software Update.' This screen shows your current iOS version and whether an update is available. If an update is available, tap 'Download and Install,' then follow the onscreen prompts.

source_refs.title: How to manually update apps from the App Store - Apple Support
source_refs.applicability: iPhone; apps downloaded from the App Store
source_refs.verified_excerpt: On your iPhone and iPad, apps that you download from the App Store automatically update by default.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On iPhone: Open the App Store app. Tap your profile photo or the 'My Account' button at the top of the screen. Tap 'App Updates.' To update one app, tap 'Update' next to it. To update everything, tap 'Update All.' On your iPhone and iPad, apps that you download from the App Store automatically update by default.

source_refs.section: Check for updates in the Settings app
source_refs.applicability: Android phone; generic Android steps, Wi-Fi and battery conditions as stated on the page
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Most system updates and security patches install automatically.

source_refs.title: How to update your Galaxy phone or tablet
source_refs.applicability: Samsung Galaxy phone or tablet; menu labels vary by model and carrier; Wi-Fi and auto download conditions as stated on the page
source_refs.verified_excerpt: If a system update is available, you should install it to keep your phone or tablet running smoothly.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Samsung Galaxy phone: Pull down from the top-right corner with two fingers, then tap the 'Settings' icon. Scroll to and tap 'Software update' or 'System updates.' The label varies by model. Tap 'Download and install,' 'Check for system updates,' or 'Check for software updates,' depending on your carrier. If an update is found, it should start downloading automatically, though some devices require you to tap 'Download now.' When the download finishes, follow the on-screen prompts to install. Some carriers may require a Wi-Fi connection to check for and install updates.

source_refs.title: Install Windows Updates | Microsoft Support
source_refs.applicability: Windows 11; Windows Update in Settings; step 2 only if updates are found; step 3 only when Windows prompts for a restart
source_refs.verified_excerpt: In Windows, you decide when and how to get the latest updates to keep your device running smoothly and securely.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Windows 11: Open 'Start,' then 'Settings,' then 'Windows Update,' and select 'Check for Windows updates.' If updates are available, select 'Download & install.' The device downloads and installs them. If prompted, restart the device to finish applying the updates.

source_refs.title: Update macOS on Mac - Apple Support
source_refs.section: Use Software Update to get updates
source_refs.applicability: Mac; System Settings; administrator password and installation conditions as stated on the page
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Software Update finds, downloads, and installs Apple software updates that are compatible with your Mac model.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Mac: Click the Apple menu in the top-left corner, then choose 'System Settings.' In the sidebar, click 'General,' then click 'Software Update' on the right. If an update is available, click the update button to install it. If no update is available, Software Update shows that your Mac is up to date. When asked, enter your administrator password (the password you use to log in to your Mac). Keep your Mac awake and its lid open until installation finishes. It may restart several times and show a progress bar or blank screen.

source_refs.title: Update your Chromebook's operating system - Chromebook Help
source_refs.applicability: Chromebook; Settings and About ChromeOS; Wi-Fi, charger and mobile data conditions as stated on the page
source_refs.verified_excerpt: To complete the update, restart your Chromebook.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Chromebook: Connect to Wi-Fi. At the bottom right, select the time, then the 'Settings' gear icon. At the bottom left, select 'About ChromeOS.' Select 'Check for updates.' If an update is found, the download starts automatically. When the download finishes, look at the bottom right, next to the date, for the 'Update device' notification and select 'Restart.' To complete the update, restart your Chromebook. Plug in the charger to avoid interruptions during the update.
